display.title: Episode 484: The Big Surprise (Summer Vacation)
display.summary_short: Taking Hashem along on summer vacation, the lesson of the Akeidah, and the story of a poor sand-seller whose stolen horse and wagon came home carrying a treasure.
display.summary_long: Broadcast as summer vacation begins, the week before Yud-Beis Tammuz. Uncle Yossi reminds children to pack their siddur and Chumash, to learn and daven every day, and to say Tehillim and the Twelve Pesukim for protection while traveling. After the Hakochainik march, a boy from a Brooklyn yeshiva says the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Uncle Yossi introduces the theme of emunah and bitachon with the Akeidah, Avraham Avinu's greatest test, which we read every morning before davening. The story follows Rabbi Yitzchak, a poor, learned man who sells fresh sand from a forest cave and still gives tzedakah every day. When a thief steals his horse and wagon in a storm, he tells his family that whatever Hashem does is for the good, and they say Tehillim. In the forest the thief finds a chest of treasure in the cave, but the sand collapses on him, and the horse brings the wagon, treasure and all, back home. The show ends with advice on choosing a kosher summer camp, the story of Yud-Beis Tammuz, when the Frierdiker Rebbe was freed from prison in Russia, and candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Trust that everything Hashem does is for the good, and keep davening and learning even when times are hard.

date.note: 'This coming Monday is Yud-Beis Tammuz' (12 Tammuz 5751 = Monday 24 June 1991); start of summer vacation; candle lighting 8:12. A Tuesday.
